answers.answer: The private invitation report gains a date for each row. Before this change, the report row showed none of it: the row ('REPORT ROW invitation', 'Synthetic Person') had a dashed DATE_ADDED cell marked 'no date'. Now the report row carries that exact timestamp as date added: the matching prospect row in Supabase (tracked-a, created_at) supplies its creation time. The slides say 'Each prospect row matched here supplies its creation time, or unknown when missing', 'Each selected invitation row then gets its date' and 'Each row now shows its date added. Unknown stays unknown.' So the reviewer of the private invitation report sees, for every row, when it was added; a bad value is never guessed and is never copied ('The row keeps a reason, and the bad value is never copied'). The packet names no audience other than the reviewer of that private invitation report; no other consumer is shown.

The only function named in the packet is _date_added, applied per row at lines 1030-1031: 'for row in rows_out:' then 'row.update(_date_added(row["profile_url"], prospect'. The packet does not name the function that encloses the other changed lines (line 453 'if len(matches) != 1:' and lines 472-476 'except (ShortlistInputError, OverflowError):' ... 'if parsed > now:' ... 'provenance["reason"] = "future_timestamp"'), so the enclosing function of that validation block is CANNOT TELL.

The new code rejects a timestamp in two ways. It catches a raising parse with 'except (ShortlistInputError, OverflowError):' then 'provenance["reason"] = "invalid_timestamp"' and returns the row as unknown: 'return {"date_added": None, "date_added_source": provenance}'. It also compares the parsed value with the current time: 'if parsed > now:' and then 'provenance["reason"] = "future_timestamp"'. So for a timestamp in the future the reason recorded is exactly 'future_timestamp', and the row stays unknown, because 'The row keeps a reason, and the bad value is never copied.' The cases slide shows '(None, "missing")', '(42, "invalid_timestamp")', '("0001-01-01T00:00:00+01:00", "invalid_timestamp")', '("9999-12-31T23:59:59-01:00", "invalid_timestamp")', '("not-a-timestamp", "invalid_timestamp")', '("2026-09-30T14:12:13", "invalid_timestamp")' and '("2026-10-03T00:00:00Z", "future_timestamp")'. The check above these is line 453, 'if len(matches) != 1:'.
